content:
Yesterday we read through the events of Numbers 8; the lighting of the seven lamps and the consecration of the Levites for their ministry. Today we slow down at the very first instruction Yahweh gave in this chapter and look at it more carefully, because there is more in it than we might first notice.

The command was simple: “When you set up the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the lampstand” (Numbers 8:2). Forward. The light was to fall forward. Not sideways, not backward, not in every direction equally; but forward. How exactly does a lamp give its light in a specific direction,
and why did Yahweh specify this? Both questions have an answer, and together they carry a message that reaches directly into our lives today.

An oil lamp in the ancient world burned through a wick; a twisted cord or strip of cloth soaked in oil that drew the fuel upward and held the flame. The most important detail about how a lamp gives its light is this: the wick determines the primary direction of the flame. The brightest part of the light comes from the wick side of the lamp. By turning the wick in a particular direction,
the priest could orient the lamp so that its strongest and brightest light fell in that specific direction. Yahweh commanded that all seven wicks be turned to face forward; toward the front of the Holy Place, toward the table of showbread and the golden altar of incense beyond it.

This was a deliberate act of the priest every time he tended the lamps. He was not simply refilling the oil and trimming the wick and leaving it to burn in any direction. He was actively positioning each lamp so that its light did not scatter aimlessly but fell purposefully forward. The Holy Place had no windows.

The only light inside was the light of the lampstand. And Yahweh wanted that light to fall forward; illuminating the path ahead, showing the table and the altar that lay in the direction of worship and approach to God. The light was not for looking backward at what had already been passed. It was for seeing what lay ahead.

In Scripture, the direction forward is consistently associated with purpose, movement, inheritance, and the journey toward what God has promised.

Psalm 119:105 says: “Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.” The light of the Word does not illuminate the road behind us. It illuminates the next step, the path ahead, the way that is still to be walked. The lamp in the Holy Place faced forward because the people of God are always moving forward; always pressing toward the promise, always walking toward the inheritance, always oriented toward what Yahweh has set before them rather than what lies behind.

Paul captured this orientation exactly in Philippians 3:13-14: “Forgetting what lies behind and straining forward to what lies ahead, I press on toward the goal for the prize of the upward call of God in Christ Jesus.” The wick is turned forward. The brightest light is not cast on the past; on old failures, old seasons, old pain, old sin already forgiven and removed. The brightest light falls forward; on the next step of obedience, the next stage of the journey,
the promise that is still ahead. Abraham is the perfect picture of this.
Hebrews 11:10 says he was looking for a city that has foundations,
whose designer and builder is God. His eyes were always forward.
And Hebrews 12:2 calls us to fix our eyes on Jesus; forward, toward the one who sits at the right hand of the Father, the one the whole journey is leading toward.

The lampstand had seven lamps; not one, not three, but seven. Seven is the number of fullness and completeness in Scripture. Seven lamps burning together on one lampstand speak of the complete, full, sufficient light of Yahweh illuminating His house. And Revelation 4:5 gives us a window into what this fullness means in the heavenly reality: “From the throne came flashes of lightning, and rumblings and peals of thunder, and before the throne were burning seven torches of fire, which are the seven spirits of God.” Seven torches before the throne. And Isaiah 11:2 names these seven spirits precisely as they rested on the Messiah: the Spirit of Yahweh, the Spirit of wisdom, the Spirit of understanding, the Spirit of counsel, the Spirit of might, the Spirit of knowledge, and the Spirit of the fear of Yahweh. Seven dimensions of the full, complete light of God; all seven turned forward, all seven shining in the same direction.

This means that when we walk forward in the light of the Spirit, we are walking in all seven of these together. We walk forward with wisdom that is from above, not the wisdom of the past age we have left behind. We walk forward with understanding; the ability to discern what God is doing now and where He is leading next. We walk forward with counsel that comes from the Spirit rather than from our own calculations. We walk forward with might that is not ours; a strength that carries us through the hard ground of the journey ahead.

We walk forward with knowledge of Yahweh deepening with every step.
And we walk forward with the fear of Yahweh; the reverence that keeps our feet on the right path and our eyes on the right prize. Seven lamps. All forward. All together.

The lamp in Numbers 8 was not lit for the priest’s own benefit alone. It lit the entire Holy Place so that the work of the sanctuary could be done. The table of showbread could only be set properly because the lampstand gave its light.

The golden altar of incense could only be approached because the lampstand gave its light. Without the lamps forward and burning, nothing else in the Holy Place could function as it was designed to. In the same way, the new creation believer does not carry the light only for personal spiritual comfort. The light is given to illuminate the path for others as well. Matthew 5:14-16 says: “You are the light of the world. A city set on a hill cannot be hidden. Let your light shine before others, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in heaven.” The lamp does not shine toward itself. It shines outward, forward, for the benefit of those in the room.

For ourselves, the lesson is to keep the wick turned forward. When the enemy tries to turn our attention backward; to old regrets, old wounds, old failures, old seasons of defeat; we must return the wick to its position. The light of the Word and the Spirit in us is not given for rehearsing the past. It is given for seeing the next step. Proverbs 4:18 says: “The path of the just is as the shining light, that shines more and more unto the perfect day.” More and more.

The light does not diminish as the journey continues. It grows brighter as we press forward. The perfect day; the day of full and complete light, the day when faith gives way to sight and the lampstand gives way to the Lamb who is the light of the City (Rev 21:23). The new creation does not hide the truth. It shines it to the Church, to the world, and to everyone who is searching for the light of Yahweh. Seven lamps. All forward. Shining more and more unto the perfect day.

title: Prayer
text: Yahweh, You are the Father of lights, and in You there is no darkness at all (1 John 1:5). You commanded the seven lamps to face forward because You are always leading Your people forward; toward the promise, toward the Kingdom, toward the perfect day. We thank You for the full light of Your seven Spirits, Your spirit, wisdom, understanding, counsel, might, knowledge, and the fear of Yahweh; all shining together, all turned in the same direction, all illuminating the path ahead. Forgive us for the times we have turned the wick backward dwelling on old failures, old pain, old seasons You have already redeemed and moved us through. Turn our wicks forward again today. Help us to forget what lies behind and strain forward to what lies ahead. Help us to let the light fall not just on our own path but on the paths of those around us who are searching for the next step in the dark. May we shine more and more unto the perfect day. In Christ’s name, amen.
